metadata.title: Common Shade active and system-level cooling library
metadata.review_type: Structured rapid evidence map, not an exhaustive systematic review, meta-analysis or commissioned engineering assessment
metadata.counting_unit: Distinct technology, operating configuration, service/finance mechanism, policy or monitoring function; functions are not additive cooling effects. Policies, monitoring, cold-chain adjuncts and personal cooling protocols are not all powered coolers.
metadata.evidence_basis_note: Evidence status measured can describe a study/analysis; effect.basis separately distinguishes measured, modelled, reported and qualitative guidance. A numerical claim being recorded does not independently validate it.
metadata.missing_data: Null means not verified/not publicly disclosed, not zero. Unknown cost, power, GWP, service life or income shares were not estimated.
metadata.scope_limits: Examples include historical reports, component studies, prototypes and policy jurisdictions. Two documented contexts is not two physical deployments or independent evaluations. Full installed costs, running costs, upkeep and income shares remain sparse.
metadata.clinical_note: Fan evidence is population-, humidity-, duration- and activity-specific. Public guidance and trials are kept separate; no universal safe cutoff, WBGT clearance or medical advice is generated.
metadata.no_endorsement: Listing an organisation, technology or product does not imply partnership or endorsement. No organisation is ranked.

active_solutions.name: Powered direct evaporative air cooler

mechanism.text: A fan draws air through wet media; evaporating water removes sensible heat from that air and adds moisture. A pump is common, though designs vary.

suits.reason: Best suited to hot-dry hours; insufficient wet-bulb depression limits cooling in humid weather and the device adds humidity. Do not recommend as a sealed-room substitute for humid-climate AC.
suits.interpretation: Engineering transfer judgement; not universal performance certification.

effect.result: Field measurements and occupant surveys informed local comfort zones; no isolated air-temperature reduction against an untreated baseline is claimed.
effect.date: 2019 publication; two summer seasons; exact calendar years not recovered
effect.sample: 1554 survey datasets across 10 offices using direct and one two-stage system
effect.baseline: Existing evaporatively cooled offices; not a randomised no-cooling control
effect.limitations: Repeated surveys may include same participants. Desk-work comfort, not occupational heat safety.

active_solutions.name: Indirect/dew-point evaporative cooling

mechanism.text: Water evaporates in a separate working-air stream and cools supply air through a heat exchanger, avoiding direct moisture addition to that supply stream. Regenerative/dew-point designs use different airflow arrangements.

suits.reason: Most useful in hot-dry conditions; humid-climate standalone capacity is constrained and it does not remove the supply-air moisture load. Two-stage indirect/direct devices do add moisture in the direct stage.
suits.interpretation: Engineering transfer judgement; not universal performance certification.

active_solutions.name: Worksite WBGT monitoring linked to heat protection

mechanism.text: Measure worksite heat load with a wet-bulb globe temperature assessment and use it with workload, clothing/PPE, acclimatisation and worker condition to select protective actions. WBGT is an environmental index, not body temperature, ordinary weather wet-bulb temperature or a guarantee of safety.

suits.reason: Monitoring and response controls apply in both climates, but measured conditions and local response rules differ. This measure itself does not cool air or people.

effect.result: Worksite monitoring is an input to exposure reduction and response. No standalone reduction in temperature, injury or mortality attributable solely to a WBGT meter was verified.
